articles.title: BeamGAN: a physics-informed conditional generative adversarial network for Monte-Carlo-free portal dose image prediction from incident fluence maps
articles.summary: Researchers developed BeamGAN, a physics-informed deep learning framework capable of predicting portal dose images directly from treatment planning system fluence maps. This tool aims to facilitate real-time patient-specific quality assurance without the need for intensive Monte Carlo simulations.

articles.title: Clinical outcomes and quality of life after proton therapy for cranial and extracranial solitary fibrous tumors
articles.summary: This study evaluated the efficacy and safety of proton therapy for treating cranial and extracranial solitary fibrous tumors. Preliminary results indicate promising overall survival and local control rates, although late toxicities near the central nervous system warrant clinical vigilance.

articles.title: Design, implementation, and assessment of an independent second-check system for proton and carbon-ion pencil-beam scanning
articles.summary: Researchers implemented a unified platform for independent verification of physical and RBE-weighted doses in ion beam therapy. The study highlights the need for continued multicase validation to ensure robust clinical implementation of this second-check workflow.

articles.title: Cone-beam CT-based synthetic CT generation for adaptive radiotherapy: methodological paradigms, clinical reliability assessment, and translation
articles.summary: This review examines deep learning approaches for generating synthetic CT images from cone-beam CT to facilitate adaptive radiotherapy. It assesses the current limitations in image accuracy and reliability for patient-specific dosimetry in both photon and proton therapy environments.

articles.title: Development of a phantom-based end-to-end QA workflow for online adaptive radiotherapy incorporating high-resolution 2D detector measurements
articles.summary: This study introduces a feasible end-to-end quality assurance workflow for Ethos online adaptive radiotherapy platforms. The method utilizes high-resolution 2D measurements to effectively identify plan-specific deviations during the adaptation process.

articles.title: Therapeutic Hybrid Intelligence with Neural and Knowledge-based Expert Reasoning for SRS (THINKERS): an AI model for melanoma brain metastases
articles.summary: This study introduces an AI-driven framework for patient-specific stereotactic radiosurgery dose comparison. The model demonstrated feasibility as an adjunct for evaluating radiosurgical plans in patients with melanoma brain metastases.

articles.title: A virtual physicist framework integrating dose prediction and large language models for automated treatment planning
articles.summary: This study demonstrates that integrating dose prediction with LLM-driven optimization enables a robust, fully automated planning workflow. The approach improves OAR sparing and consistency without compromising target dose quality, showing potential for intelligent clinical radiotherapy planning.

articles.title: Clinical application of MR-Only in cyberknife stereotactic radiotherapy for brain metastases: a feasibility study
articles.summary: Researchers verified the feasibility of an MR-only workflow for CyberKnife stereotactic radiotherapy by generating accurate synthetic CT images for brain metastases. This method supports the reduction of CT-based imaging requirements in clinical workflows.

articles.title: The consolidation paradox: rethinking thoracic radiotherapy in extensive-stage small cell lung cancer in the immunotherapy era
articles.summary: This analysis re-examines the role of consolidative thoracic radiotherapy in extensive-stage small cell lung cancer. The study highlights the uncertainty of incorporating radiotherapy alongside modern chemo-immunotherapy protocols given the evolving clinical landscape.

articles.title: Interpatient and intrapatient variability in organ absorbed doses during [177Lu]Lu-DOTATATE therapy for neuroendocrine tumors
articles.summary: Research indicates significant variability in organ absorbed doses during PRRT, supporting the need for personalized dosimetry. The findings suggest that fixed-activity protocols may be insufficient for optimizing safety and efficacy in molecular radiotherapy.

articles.title: BayCare Proton Center Treats First Patient on Mevion S250 FIT™ with Leo Cancer Care's Marie® Solution
articles.summary: BayCare Health System has successfully treated its first patient at the new St. Joseph's Hospital proton therapy center. The facility utilizes the Mevion S250 FIT proton therapy system integrated with Leo Cancer Care's Marie upright patient positioning solution.

articles.title: Relative transmitted-dose reduction of 3D-printed and elastomeric dental radiotherapy spacers at different thicknesses
articles.summary: This investigation evaluated how material type and thickness of dental radiotherapy spacers influence radiation dose reduction. The results highlight that while materials provide protection, the effect is modest and setup-specific, requiring careful consideration in clinical practice.

articles.title: Case Report: Neurosurgery, octreotide, cabergoline, radiotherapy, pasireotide and pegvisomant - a multimodal strategy for adolescent acrogigantism
articles.summary: This case report details a complex, multidisciplinary treatment strategy for adolescent acrogigantism. It illustrates the role of radiotherapy as part of a multimodal approach for rare and invasive pediatric pituitary neuroendocrine tumors.

articles.title: Spatially adaptive dose-grid method for efficient proton therapy optimization involving small or irregular structures
articles.summary: Researchers introduced a novel spatially adaptive grid-based proton dose calculation and treatment planning method. The approach improves accuracy and efficiency for clinical cases involving small or irregular organs at risk and targets.

articles.title: Deep learning-based automated segmentation of target volumes for pediatric craniospinal irradiation in proton therapy
articles.summary: This study demonstrates that a deep learning-based automated segmentation model can achieve accurate target delineation for pediatric craniospinal irradiation in proton therapy. The findings suggest that integrating such frameworks into clinical workflows can improve efficiency, reproducibility, and standardization of treatment planning.

articles.title: Pelvic bone marrow dosimetry predicts grade 2 hematologic adverse events in locally advanced rectal cancer
articles.summary: This study establishes dosimetric constraints for pelvic bone marrow to reduce the risk of grade 2 or higher hematologic adverse events in rectal cancer patients undergoing neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy. The findings provide practical quantitative references for improving bone marrow sparing in pelvic radiation oncology.

articles.title: From synthesis to clinic: a task-specific framework for CT images metal artifact reduction in cervical brachytherapy
articles.summary: Researchers developed a task-specific deep learning framework to reduce metal artifacts in CT scans used for cervical brachytherapy. The model showed improved geometric accuracy, supporting its potential to enhance clinical workflow efficiency and precision in brachytherapy planning.

articles.title: Combining handcrafted radiomics features and deep learning features within different regions of interest in planning CT images for the prediction of symptomatic radiation pneumonitis in locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer
articles.summary: A hybrid predictive model combining radiomics and deep learning was developed and externally validated to predict symptomatic radiation pneumonitis in non-small cell lung cancer patients. The study highlights the clinical potential of utilizing combined features to improve the predictive performance of toxicity modeling.

articles.title: BayCare Proton Center Treats First Patient on Mevion S250 FIT™ with Leo Cancer Care's Marie® Solution
articles.summary: The BayCare Proton Center has successfully initiated patient treatments using the Mevion S250 FIT proton therapy system integrated with Leo Cancer Care's Marie solution. This facility represents a new implementation of compact proton therapy technology.

articles.title: Experimental verification of clinical dose and LET maps for LET-informed proton therapy
articles.summary: This study introduces an optically stimulated luminescence film-based detector system to verify spatially resolved dose and dose-averaged linear energy transfer distributions. This methodology supports the clinical translation of LET-informed proton therapy beyond conventional constant-RBE assumptions.

articles.title: Review of radiobiological dose rate effects at the edge between conventional and FLASH
articles.summary: This review examines dose rate effects within the 0.4-35 Gy/s range, noting that while traditional models view these as negligible, the transition to active pencil beam scanning and the emergence of ultra-high dose rate radiotherapy warrant further investigation into radiobiological impacts.

articles.title: Preliminary Feasibility and Dosimetric Evaluation of Retroperitoneal Hydrogel Spacer Placement for Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy
articles.summary: This cadaveric study demonstrates that CT-guided hydrogel spacer placement in the perirenal space is technically feasible and may reduce bowel radiation dose during stereotactic body radiation therapy for renal cell carcinoma. Further validation is required for broader clinical implementation.

articles.title: Radiotherapy for Cervical Cancer: Technical Advances, Clinical Applications, and Future Perspectives
articles.summary: This review summarizes recent technological developments in external beam radiotherapy and brachytherapy for cervical cancer treatment. It covers evolutions in image guidance and delivery systems with a focus on clinical translation and international practice standards.

articles.title: Dose-rate metrics for ionization-chamber recombination in synchrotron-based ultra-high-dose-rate proton and carbon-ion beams: application and validity of quasi-static response models
articles.summary: This study evaluates different dose-rate metrics to predict saturation correction factors in ultra-high-dose-rate (UHDR) proton and carbon-ion beams. Researchers compared field-averaged and pencil-beam-scanning dose rates to improve dosimetry accuracy for emerging radiotherapy modalities.

articles.title: Comparative evaluation of plan robustness in proton and photon radiotherapy in deep inspiration breath-hold for mediastinal lymphomas throughout the treatment course
articles.summary: This study compares the robustness of pencil beam scanning proton therapy and volumetric modulated arc therapy for mediastinal lymphoma using deep inspiration breath-hold. The findings suggest proton therapy offers superior sparing of organs at risk while maintaining consistent target coverage.

articles.title: Preliminary Dose Constraints for Testing Intensity Modulated Proton Therapy in Anal Cancer Trials
articles.summary: Researchers have developed specific dose-volume constraints for intensity modulated proton therapy (IMPT) in the context of anal cancer. These guidelines aim to facilitate future clinical trials by reducing dose spill to healthy tissue compared to standard photon approaches.

articles.title: Cardio-respiratory-gated proton pencil beam scanning for cardiac ablation: workflow and end-to-end validation
articles.summary: This research validates a new workflow for cardiorespiratory-gated proton beam delivery for cardiac ablation. The system demonstrated rapid response times to motion, enabling significant reduction in target expansion volumes during treatment planning.

articles.title: Artificial intelligence in esophageal cancer radiotherapy: a literature review
articles.summary: This review examines the integration of artificial intelligence into esophageal cancer radiotherapy, highlighting its potential to enhance workflow efficiency and treatment accuracy. The authors emphasize the need for prospective, multicenter studies to ensure clinical translation and reliability.

articles.title: Predicting acute radiation dermatitis in breast cancer patients using artificial intelligence: a systematic review
articles.summary: This systematic review analyzes current AI-based models for predicting acute radiation dermatitis in breast cancer treatment. While results are promising, the study notes that a lack of standardized reporting and external validation currently limits clinical implementation.

articles.title: Survey of Respiratory Motion Management Practices in Particle Therapy Facilities in Japan
articles.summary: This study details the implementation and technical trends of respiratory motion management in particle therapy across Japanese institutions. It provides insight into the diverse strategies currently employed for motion-sensitive dose distribution in proton therapy.

articles.title: Unintended coverage: how standard breast radiotherapy irradiates the internal mammary nodes
articles.summary: This research analyzes internal mammary node coverage during standard breast radiotherapy using tangential fields. The findings emphasize the clinical need for explicit contouring and dedicated planning when coverage of these nodes is indicated.

articles.title: The measure that matters: What medicine asks of artificial intelligence
articles.summary: This position paper highlights a misalignment between current AI evaluation metrics and clinical value. It urges the field to focus on outcomes that impact patient survival rather than subspecialist preference.
